app.title: PHOENIX STL Studio
parts.empty:
Drop STL files here
or press Open
printer.label: Printer
cut.none: Select a part in the list
cut.open_warning: The model was open where it was cut. Run Auto Repair on the new parts.
export.note: Binary STL in millimetres. Opens directly in Elegoo SatelLite, Chitubox and Lychee.
export.overwrite: {n} file(s) already exist in this folder. Overwrite?
err.memory: Not enough free memory (needs about {need} GB, {avail} GB free). Close other programs, or cut the model into smaller parts first.
err.no_cut: The plane doesn't cut through this part.
err.crashed: The engine stopped unexpectedly ({detail}). Your parts are safe, please try again.
msg.problems: {name} has problems. Open the Repair tab and press Auto Repair.
rename.title: Rename part
printer.name: Name
move.info: Size {x} × {y} × {z} mm · lowest point Z = {zmin} mm
move.hint: Drag the selected part in the 3D view to slide it on the bed. Hold Shift while dragging to move it up or down.
move.pick_face: Click the face that should lie on the bed (Esc to cancel)
move.laid_flat: Face turned to the bed. Press Apply to keep it.
err.not_solid: Merge needs closed solids. Run Auto Repair on the parts first, or use Combine.
cut.hint_plane: One flat cut. Drag the orange plane in the view or type the values.
cut.hint_grid: Cuts the part into a grid of pieces in one go. Fit to Printer chooses the fewest pieces that fit your printer.
cut.hint_curve: Press Draw, then click points on the model in the view. Shift+click makes a sharp corner, Backspace removes the last point, Enter finishes. The line is extended straight past the model and cuts through it in the viewing direction.
cut.hint_freeform: The plane above is the base. Click an orange control point in the view and drag it to bend the cutting surface.
cut.fit_done: Planes set for {n} pieces. Move any plane before cutting if you like.
cut.grid_empty: Add at least one plane (more than 1 piece along an axis).
cut.curve_empty: Draw a line with at least 2 points first.
cut.free_none: Click a control point in the view
err.not_solid_cut: This cut needs a closed solid. Run Auto Repair on the part first.
cut.grid_none: No planes yet: set more than 1 piece along an axis, or press Fit to printer.
conn.none: Select two touching parts, or one part and then pick its flat face.
conn.hint: Two parts cut apart: their shared face is found automatically. One part: press Pick flat face and click the face. Drag the orange dots to move connectors.
conn.picking: Click a flat face of the part in the view…
conn.hollow: · hollow part: solid bosses are added where the wall is thin
conn.note_dowel: Holes in both parts; the pins are made as a separate part to print.
conn.note_peg: A peg grows out of one part and fits a hole in the other.
conn.note_magnet: Matching holes in both parts. Glue the magnets in with opposite poles facing.
conn.note_rod: Holes in both parts for a brass/steel rod cut to the length set here.
conn.note_key: A square peg: the parts cannot turn, even with a single key.
conn.note_tongue: A rim on one part fits a groove in the other, all around the joint. Seals and aligns.
conn.note_dovetail: A wedge-shaped rail that slides into a matching channel and cannot pull out sideways.
conn.pins_note: {n} pins will be added as a separate part.
conn.outside: That point is outside the joint face.
conn.coupon_hint: Print a small plate with 5 holes (gaps around the current value) and a test pin, to find the right gap for your printer and resin.
conn.coupon_info: Gaps of holes 1–5 (hole k has k dots): {list} mm. Push the pin into each hole and choose the one that fits the way you want.
conn.coupon_done: Tolerance coupon added: print it with the pin.
conn.saved: Saved {c} mm as the "{fit}" gap for {printer}.
conn.no_room: No connectors to add. Place some (automatically or by clicking), or choose a smaller size.
err.no_joint: These parts do not share a flat face. Select two parts that were cut apart, or use Pick flat face.
err.no_face: No flat face there. Click on a flat (cut) face.
conn.again: These connectors were just added. Change a setting (or press Place automatically) to add more.
mold.none: Select the model to make a silicone mold of.
mold.hint: A printed shell around the model at an exact distance: pour silicone into the gap. Put the model on the bed first (Move tab). Drag the orange dot (pour) and blue dots (vents) to move them.
mold.plate: Base plate (the model stands on it)
mold.done: Mold built: about {ml} ml of silicone
mold.warn_sprue_outside: The pour hole is not above the cavity; it was left out. Move the orange dot over the model.
mold.warn_sprue_blocked: Something of the mold is above the pour hole; check that pouring is possible there.
mold.warn_vent_skipped: A vent was left out: it is not above the cavity, or another part of the mold is in the way.
err.mold_failed: The mold could not be built. Try another quality, a thicker wall, or Auto Repair on the model first.
